candidate.answerReason: The denominator must be a positive proper divisor of 30. The seven possibilities are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, and 15.

methods.label: Turn the denominator into a divisor
methods.explanation:
Because \(n\) is positive, the quotient can be positive only when its denominator is positive. Thus \(0<n<30\). The value \(n=30\) is undefined, and larger values give a negative quotient.

Let \(d=30-n\). Then \(d\) is an integer with \(1\le d<30\), and
\[
\frac{n}{30-n}
=\frac{30-d}{d}
=\frac{30}{d}-1.
\]
This is an integer exactly when \(d\) divides 30. For every positive divisor \(d<30\), it is also positive.

The factor pairs of 30 are \((1,30)\), \((2,15)\), \((3,10)\), and \((5,6)\). Excluding 30 leaves the seven divisors
\[
1,2,3,5,6,10,15.
\]
Each gives exactly one value \(n=30-d\), and different divisors give different values of \(n\). Hence there are \(\boxed{7}\) positive integers, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: A sign restriction and a short divisor list completely determine the solutions; prime-exponent formulas are not needed.
